concepts.name: Carbonyl Nucleophilic Addition & Ammonia Derivatives
concepts.summary: Nucleophilic addition to $>\text{C=O}$: addition of $\text{HCN}$ gives cyanohydrins, addition of $\text{NaHSO}_3$ gives crystalline bisulphite adducts. Reaction with ammonia derivatives $\text{H}_2\text{N-Z}$ eliminates water to give crystalline derivatives (oximes with $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$, hydrazones with $\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$, 2,4-DNP derivatives).
concepts.common_traps: In semicarbazide $\text{H}_2\text{N-CO-NH-NH}_2$, only the hydrazine $\text{NH}_2$ reacts; the amide $\text{NH}_2$ is deactivated by resonance with $>\text{C=O}$.

concepts.name: Named Condensation Reactions & Diagnostic Tests
concepts.summary: Aldol condensation requires $\alpha$-hydrogen. Cannizzaro occurs for aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-H (disproportionation into alcohol + carboxylate). Iodoform test: positive for compounds containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ group. Tollens' & Fehling's tests oxidize aldehydes, not ketones.
concepts.common_traps: Acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$) gives positive iodoform test, while benzophenone does not.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Clemmensen uses acidic conditions (Zn-Hg / conc. HCl); Wolff-Kishner uses basic conditions ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$ / KOH / glycol).

### 2.1 Carbonyl Nucleophilic Addition & Ammonia Derivatives (Reactions & Mechanisms)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **12 PYQs** (High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Nucleophilic addition to $>	ext{C=O}$: addition of $\text{HCN}$ gives cyanohydrins, addition of $\text{NaHSO}_3$ gives crystalline bisulphite adducts. Reaction with ammonia derivatives $\text{H}_2\text{N-Z}$ eliminates water to give crystalline derivatives (oximes with $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$, hydrazones with $\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$, 2,4-DNP derivatives).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
>\text{C=O} + \text{H}_2\text{N-Z} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} >\text{C=N-Z} + \text{H}_2\text{O}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: In semicarbazide $\text{H}_2\text{N-CO-NH-NH}_2$, only the hydrazine $\text{NH}_2$ reacts; the amide $\text{NH}_2$ is deactivated by resonance with $>	ext{C=O}$.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Reactivity order toward nucleophilic addition: $\text{HCHO} > \text{RCHO} > \text{RCOR}$.

- **[2025 Shift] Q#4 (MCQ)**: *"Oxidation of Toluene with chromyl chloride followed by hydrolysis gives Benzaldehyde. This reaction is known as ____________..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Named Condensation Reactions & Diagnostic Tests (Named Reactions & Tests)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **11 PYQs** (High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Aldol condensation requires $\alpha$-hydrogen. Cannizzaro occurs for aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-H (disproportionation into alcohol + carboxylate). Iodoform test: positive for compounds containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ group. Tollens' & Fehling's tests oxidize aldehydes, not ketones.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
2\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCHO}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Acetophenone ($	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5	ext{COCH}_3$) gives positive iodoform test, while benzophenone does not.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Clemmensen uses acidic conditions (Zn-Hg / conc. HCl); Wolff-Kishner uses basic conditions ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$ / KOH / glycol).

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Aldehyde and Ketone

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
